subject: Duplicating ggplot2 in the same code

messages.author: 309910fa4717b4a3
messages.subject: Duplicating ggplot2 in the same code
parts:
Using ggplot2 in my R code, I create two identical plots in two different places in the code. Only data, annotate and labs change. I was wondering if there's a way to reuse the layer portion. That way I don't duplicate code and if I decide to change colors I only need to do it in one place.

The ggplot2 code that repeats is:

p + layer(geom="line") +
  scale_x_discrete(labels = lbls) +
  
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(face=NULL, color=NULL,
                                   size=12, angle=90),
        axis.text.y = element_text(face="bold", color=NULL,
                                   size=14, angle=NULL)) +
  
  geom_vline(xintercept = seq(13, 157, 24), colour = "dodgerblue", linetype = "longdash") +
  
  geom_vline(xintercept = seq(25, 145, 24), colour = "blue") +


[...some annotation and some label])

messages.author: 373beb702917b8b5
messages.subject: Re: Duplicating ggplot2 in the same code
parts:
Untested because I'm on my phone, but I'm pretty sure you can do

l = layer(geom="line") +

scale_x_discrete(labels = lbls) +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(face=NULL, color=NULL,
                                   size=12, angle=90),
        axis.text.y = element_text(face="bold", color=NULL,
                                   size=14, angle=NULL)) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = seq(13, 157, 24), colour = "dodgerblue", linetype = "longdash") +
  geom_vline(xintercept = seq(25, 145, 24), colour = "blue")

ggplot(foo) + l

Best,
Ista

messages.author: 0c39e60ddb38622b
messages.subject: Re: Duplicating ggplot2 in the same code
parts:
I like Ista's suggestion (not that he needs my imprimatur :), but
another way would be to write a function whose return value is the
ggplot object (or a print thereof). Since only the data, annotation
and labels change, those could easily be passed as function arguments.
If you needed to call it multiple times, you could put the arguments
into a matrix and use mapply() (or alternatively, the m_ply() function
in the plyr package).

Dennis

As things progress and I know the extent to which the plots might vary from project to project, I might move to Dennis's suggestion.

bin.dates<-paste0("daily_clim.bin.",format(seq.Date(start.date,stop.date,1),"%Y%m%d"),".gz");length(bin.dates)
rowname <- substr(seq(as.Date("2000-01-01"),as.Date("2000-12-31"),by = 1),6,10)
years <- paste0(1983:2015);length(years)
##----Extracting the Binary Files
pixel <- matrix(nrow = length(rowname),ncol = length(years))
colnames(pixel) <- paste0("Yr ",years);rownames(pixel) <- c(rowname)
vec <- numeric(0)
for(bin.date in bin.dates){
  bin.read<-readBin(gunzip(bin.date,overwrite=FALSE,remove=FALSE),"double",n=1e6,size=4,endian = "big")[1]
  data <- c(vec,bin.read)
  print(bin.date)
}

antonio
